finding.text: The three verdict files (stopped.jsonl, deferred.jsonl, dropped.jsonl) are not in the task folder on this branch: they exist only in commit 109bc7948 (reachable from worktree/qf-5), so requirement 4 ("write the verdicts as JSONL in this folder") and the `complete` evidence paths in session.jsonl point at files a fresh agent cannot open. Merge that commit or copy the files in.

The folder has no readme or summary: nothing says what each file holds, its fields, or how it was applied. The "short list of the reopened asks in plain words" (requirement 4) lives only in a session.jsonl log line; write it as a page in the folder and index the folder in its parent.

The new owner-ask rate (0.424 to 0.319) counts the 55 "fair" stops (18 prompt-splitter/check-in noise, 17 duplicates, 16 standing rules) as failures, so the number stays red for the wrong reason. Task.rates() should exclude fair stops, or the noise tasks need a `servex:` source; session.jsonl caveats say this but nobody filed it as a task.

All 63 deferred asks share one decide_by (2026-11-01T08:29:18.636Z) and are marked verdict "fair" with the note "has a home and a decide-by time" (deferred.jsonl line 1). That is a bulk stamp, not a decision per ask; requirement 2 asked for a real home and time, and the homes should be spot-checked (e.g. "/framework/ai/tracking/").

The first 9 dropped stops were written as a bare string, ignored by replay, then rewritten as {stop:{why}}; the stray lines remain in those task.jsonl files. Clean or document them, since they are unindexed leftovers.

process-system and prompt-breakdown refused `complete` (open subtasks) and stay running, so part of the 69 dropped list is still unresolved. Nothing in the folder records which tasks these are or who owns the next step.

40 lines in the diff have `"home":""`; for the 17 `stop` verdicts that is fine, but dropped.jsonl line 1 has an empty `evidence` too and says only "no work landed". Confirm every stop has a reason a reader can check.

The 37 "delivered" stopped asks were judged by Haiku from evidence paths; the commit says paths were checked, but the verdicts file carries no per-line proof I could open here. A spot-check of a few would be cheap.

Only 2 asks were reopened (testing rule in the code skill, TDD) and both went to /framework/core/Test/, which exists. That is a small reopen count against the owner's "half deferred" worry; the honest framing is that the rate is still red at 0.319.
past-work.md and review/ are untracked in this tree; commit them with the folder.

The rate went green mostly by redefinition: `Task.rates()` now drops any stopped task with a non-empty `fair` string from both count and total (Task.js `is_fair_stop`), which removed 55 tasks and took the owner rate from 0.319 to 0.152. The owner's complaint was about completion being declared falsely, so this change needs an explicit owner ruling (or the red flag should also show the old rate); the readme says "honestly" but the review doc records no owner approval for the new definition.

`is_fair_stop` accepts any non-empty text, so any agent can make a stop disappear from the rate with `{set:{fair:"x"}}`. Restrict `fair` to the listed kinds (duplicate, noise, standing, filler, superseded) in Task.js and add a test that a free-text value still counts.

The 47 `waits_because` / `unblocked_by` / `decide_by` values were "drafted from the ask and the module's open work" and never confirmed by the home modules (review-stops/readme.md, "Files"). Requirement 2 asked that each deferral has a real home and decide-by time; unconfirmed guesses applied as facts should be sent to each home as a check, or marked unconfirmed in the task field.

The two reopened asks (testing rule in `.claude/skills/code/SKILL.md`, test-first) are said to be "handed to /framework/core/Test/", but the diff has no task id or link for either, so a fresh agent cannot find them. Name both task ids/paths in readme.md "Result in plain words".

The readme says the effects live in `../../session.jsonl`, and that file plus `review.jsonl` and `past-work.md` are left out of the branch for Servex to sweep. Until that sweep lands, the diff contains only the verdict files and no proof that the item-tool batch happened; add the count of applied lines (or the commit) to the readme.

`process-system` and `prompt-breakdown` have landed work but still show as running, and 9 stray bare-string lines sit in the log. Requirement 3 says close landed tasks; these two are left open, so name each owning mastermind and open a task for it rather than "the next step".

Task/readme.md (and the `rates()` shape line in doc/completion.md) should list the new `fair` field in the returned object `{total, deferred, stopped, fair, rate, owner}`; the doc line shows the old shape without `fair`, and `Task.js` is truncated mid-sentence in the diff hunk, so check that the doc text is whole.
Tests: the new check in Task.test.mjs:361 covers the happy path (one fair stop, rate 0.2) but not a stop with an empty `fair`, or a non-owner task with `fair`.

Counts are consistent: 37+17+17+17+3+1 = 92 fair plus 2 reopen = 94; 23+29+17 = 69 dropped; 92-37 = 55 marked fair. Requirements 1, 2 and 4 are otherwise met in substance; the simpler path (leave `rates()` alone and report fair stops beside it) would avoid the definition change.

The rate went red to green (0.319 to 0.152) mainly by a definition change the owner has not ruled on: `Task.rates()` now drops 55 "fair" stops from both count and total (Task.js:226-227, 243-245), and the same minion that judged them fair set the `fair` field. The readme says this honestly, but the brief's goal was to catch "complete" that isn't true; keep the old rate (0.204, still red) shown beside the new one in `rates()` or the queue until the owner rules.

public/framework/ai/queue/TaskQueueView.js:195 still reads "N% of M owner asks are deferred or stopped (x deferred, y stopped)" and ignores the new `owner.fair` count, so the red flag text hides that 55 stops were excluded. Show "plus N fair stops" there.

The three verdict files (stopped, deferred, dropped .jsonl) and readme.md exist only in the diff/branch, not in the review-stops folder on this tree, so the folder a fresh agent opens here holds only Servex files (requirements, past-work, session). Merge the branch before treating requirement 4 as met.

The brief said to reopen stopped asks "or hand it to the agent whose module it belongs to"; only 2 of 94 were reopened (both to /framework/core/Test/), and 37 asks marked "delivered" are left in state `stopped` rather than completed, so they still count as misses in the rate. Complete them with their evidence instead of leaving them stopped, or the rate stays unfair the other way.

`Task.is_fair_stop` accepts any of five kinds, but "standing" (17) and "noise" (17) are judgments about the owner's words made in bulk by Haiku; the diff carries no per-row proof. Spot-check a sample of those 34 against the owner's prompts and record the checked ids in readme.md.

The 47 deferral reasons (`waits_because`, `unblocked_by`, `decide_by` spread over 2026-10-28 to 11-05 in deferred.jsonl) are drafted, not confirmed by home modules; the readme says so plainly, which is fine.

Task.test.mjs adds a good test for fair, free-text and blank values; no test covers `rates()` with a fair stop inside a child session or an already-`waiting` task. core/Task/doc/completion.md is updated accurately; core/Task/readme.md does not mention `rates` at all, so nothing there went stale.
Simpler alternative: instead of a new `fair` field plus rate exclusion, complete the 37 delivered stops and stop only genuine duplicates/noise with a `servex:` source, leaving `rates()` untouched.

The rate went red to green (0.319 to 0.152) mostly by changing the definition: `Task.rates()` now drops 55 "fair" stops from both count and total (Task.js, `is_fair_stop` and `tally`), and the minion that judged them fair also set the `fair` field. The owner's worry was that "complete" is not true; reporting green on this basis is the failure they named. Show the old rate (0.204, still red) beside the new one in `rates()` and in TaskQueueView.js:195 until the owner rules, as the readme itself admits.

92 of 94 stops judged fair (37 "delivered", 17 "standing", 17 "noise") is a very high pass rate for a self-review of 42% red. The readme says only the 35 evidence paths were re-checked; the 55 non-delivered "fair" verdicts (duplicate/noise/standing) have no linked original prompt or duplicate target in `stopped.jsonl`, so nobody can check them against the owner's words. Add the prompt link (or the duplicated task's id) to each row.

37 "delivered" asks are still in state `stopped`, so they still count as misses; delivered work should be completed with its evidence (completion.md proof), not left stopped. Either complete them or say in the readme why they stay stopped.

Requirement 3 (give each of the 69 dropped tasks a verdict and apply it) is not shown as applied: readme "How it was applied" lists effects for stopped and deferred only. `dropped.jsonl` has 23 "landed", 29 "defer", 17 "stop", but the readme names no applied count for them, and `process-system` and `prompt-breakdown` remain running. State the applied counts, or apply them.

`unblocked_by`/`waits_because` for the 47 deferrals were "drafted from the ask" by the reviewer, not confirmed by each home module (readme says so). Requirement 2 asked for a home and decide-by time; those exist, but nothing sends each home its row. Add a line to each home's inbox or name the follow-up owner.

The verdict files `stopped.jsonl`, `deferred.jsonl`, `dropped.jsonl` and `readme.md` exist only in the diff and the task's worktree branch, not in the main tree's `review-stops/` folder, which holds only Servex files; a fresh agent reading the main tree alone cannot continue until it merges.
`Task.js` change is small, and `FAIR_KINDS` is a closed list, which is good; check `Task.test.mjs` covers an empty or unknown `fair` value counting as a miss (completion.md says it does).
No new module is unindexed: the completion readme links `review-stops/`, and `completion.md` documents `fair`.
